body:
From reproducing your steps, I found that this can be reproduced in simpler steps: - Open Godot; Project Manager or Editor, doesn't matter which - Move the arrangement of any display in `Settings>System>Display`, so that the display currently occupied by Godot is not situated in the top-left. Below is a little graphic I made for intuition. ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2fc3ab34-da31-45d5-b618-1c90af11676d) Subsequent ways to fix this involve: - Minimizing and and reopening the window - Maximizing the window - Dragging the window around - Resizing the window on the left-side, top-side; including the three corners these sides connect to; the other two sides and corner do not affect the state of this bug My intuition tells me that the internal mouse position is not updated after Windows changes the location of the display in the desktop environment. But to test this is up to someone who knows how to do that stuff. I have found that this bug is unrelated to any settings inside `Settings>System>Display>Scale & Layout`, so it is safe to say we can rule out any correlation between this bug and code related to those settings. To test this I opened the Project Manager and changed the display resolution in from 1920x1080 (my full-res) to something smaller, like 1680x1050 and 800x600, flipped the orientation around, and also changed the scale. As well as combining several of them. It yielded to abnormal results, and functions fine. This is also unrelated to what refresh rate. That might sound like a given but I thought I'd try it anyways for the record. Finally, some interesting behavior I fail to explain is visible in the embed underneath. After reproducing these steps and hovering over a selectable element, such as a LineEdit node, it shows the correct cursor icon. However, the Button nodes in the list also think they are being hovered. And in the top-right, the tool-tip pops up as if the cursor were in reality there. I am genuinely perplexed...
The embed in question
technical info: Godot v4.4.1.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3070 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6119) - 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-11800H @ 2.30GHz (16 threads)
I can confirm the bug, still reproducible in v4.5.rc1.official [6c9aa4c7d]. Reverting pr #67791 fixes the issue. CC @Sauermann
